correctness.rationale: For all B>0 and v in (0,1], derivative signs and the unimodal stationary factor reduce global maximizers to y=0 and the upper stationary branch. At any stationary point the exact objective difference is vH(y). Its derivative is strictly positive above 1/2, with H(1/2)<0<H(1), establishing a unique crossover, all ties and the universal jump. Strict monotonicity of B=2y-log(vy) above 1/2 yields the unique subsequent equal-allocation threshold B=2/v. A standalone 75,621-assertion finite script passed; global proofs are analytic.

value.rationale: Early fruiting after one versus multiple visits is an empirically motivated distinction (Cane and Schiffhauer 2003; Stavert et al. 2020). In the exact two-target benchmark, the size of the nonzero optimum activation jump is independent of target value while its budget trigger shifts logarithmically, and the initially disadvantaged flower later takes the majority of effort. These are natural, not arbitrarily sliced, allocation boundaries not implied by homogeneous-target comparisons; no claim of field-policy calibration.
